Refinery.name: Volatiles Refinery
Refinery.description:
Rock in, useful stock out. This {2} x {2} refinery weighs {0:F0} kg and draws {1:F0} kW while working. Load a block of hydrates, clay hydrates, carbon ore or meteoric iron; an ammonium salt crust; or leached residue from a Lixivar LC-3. Four nickel-iron ingots with one carbon stock make nickel steel. One carbon stock lets it split stored methane into carbon black and hydrogen; one carbon black burns with stored oxygen to make carbon dioxide. Four spent CO2 scrubber cartridges or EVA filters give three working ones back.

Collect solids from the tray. Link a water silo and the gas stores the batch needs, touching the refinery or on its water or gas line. It waits for any required gas store. The room gets hot, and carbon ore and salt crust release gas into its air: keep a scrubber running. A melt kept waiting for a cool room too long freezes into slag.

Material.PhobosNickelIronIngot_descripti: A 4 kg ingot cast from meteoric iron as it comes: iron with a few percent of nickel and a trace of cobalt. Sound structural stock for machining, and the feed for nickel steel. Not steel by itself.
Material.PhobosNickelSteelIngot_descript: A 4 kg ingot of nickel steel, carburised in the refinery from four nickel-iron ingots and a kilogram of carbon. Tougher than plain steel and worth more: the best thing a lump of meteoric iron can become aboard.
Material.PhobosCarbonBlack_description: A kilogram of fine soot-black carbon, cracked out of methane in the refinery. Burn it there with stored oxygen for carbon dioxide your crops can use, or sell it; it is worth little.
Material.PhobosExhaustedSorbent_descript: The scrubber cartridge that could not be saved: one in four is lost when the refinery restores used cartridges. Its shell and spent gas-absorbing material cannot be recovered.
Material.PhobosPlantAsh_description: The pinch of mineral ash a straw bale leaves when the refinery burns or chars it. Nothing more comes out of it; carry it out of the tray and sell or discard it.
Material.PhobosSpentMash_description: What is left in the vats after a fermenter-still charge: pulp, yeast and sugar that did not ferment. Nothing more comes out of it; carry it out of the tray and sell or discard it.
Material.PhobosAlembrineSpirit_descripti: A 35 g measure of clear spirit at 40% alcohol, bottled aboard from your own beets. It drinks like any other liquor: a lift for morale, a hazard for judgement. Not for the reactor.
Material.PhobosCarbonStock_description: One kilogram of carbon driven out of carbon ore in the refinery. Melted in excess with four nickel-iron ingots it makes nickel steel; alone, with a methane store linked, it is the bed that cracks methane into carbon black and hydrogen.
Material.PhobosRefinerySlag_description: A kilogram of dirty leftovers skimmed from a metal melt, or a frozen batch broken out of the hearth. Nothing more can be recovered from it.
Material.PhobosAnhydrousResidue_descript: Eight kilograms of baked clay with its water driven off. Nothing more can be recovered from it.
Material.PhobosClayHydrates_description: A chunk of dark, water-rich clay minerals of the kind sampled from carbonaceous asteroids, about a fifth of it bound water. Bake it in a refinery for water; the government kiosks buy it like other ore.

Sabatier.name: Sabatier Reactor
Sabatier.description: Get some of the crew's water back from scrubbed CO2. This 2 x 2 reactor weighs {0:F0} kg and uses a catalyst to turn carbon dioxide and hydrogen into methane and water (CO2 + 4 H2 -> CH4 + 2 H2O). Each one-hour cycle draws {1:F1} kW and takes {2:F3} kg of hydrogen from a linked store and {3:F3} kg of CO2 from an installed canister within one tile. Link a water silo for its {4:F3} kg of water and a methane store for its {5:F3} kg of methane. The reaction warms the room. Run it with an X2 to recover about half the water used to make the hydrogen.

Manifold.name: RCS Propellant Manifold
Manifold.description: A {0:F0} kg valve block needing no power that feeds your RCS thrusters from bulk gas stores. Install it where a gas canister would go, on one of an RCS Intake Regulator's gas-input tiles. Link gas stores within one tile, or along a gas line that runs under or right beside both, switch each one on, and choose whether the thrusters draw from the manifold before or after the regulator's own canisters. Every gas pushes by its own worth: a kilogram of methane gives about 1.45 times the push of nitrogen, hydrogen about 3.7 times. Everything starts switched off.

Regulator.name: Cabin Air Regulator
Regulator.description:
Keep the room's air topped up. This {0:F0} kg regulator draws {1:F1} kW. It adds oxygen from a linked store at up to {2:F0} kg an hour until it reaches your chosen level. If you set a room pressure, it then adds nitrogen at up to {3:F0} kg an hour.

It stops adding gas below {4:F0} kPa, when the room may be open to space. Oxygen is capped at {5:F0}% because rich air makes fires worse. Leach.name: Leach and Crystallise Unit
Leach.description:
Wash useful salts out of rock, then mix them into plant feed. This {2} x {2} unit weighs {0:F0} kg, draws {1:F0} kW and warms its room. Choose a recipe and load its supplies.

Evaporite crust gives potassium sulfate, phosphate concentrate, washed residue for the refinery and waste salt cake. Mix the concentrate with ammonia and water for struvite fertiliser. Olivine ore, sulfuric acid and water give Epsom salt. One phosphoric acid flask, three Epsom salt and ammonia give three struvite and three ammonium sulfate. With Phobos Agriculture installed, it also mixes Groundwork makeup salts, or one each of the four salts with ammonia and acid into crop nutrients.

Link the water silo, ammonia store and acid tank your recipe needs, touching the unit or on the matching line. Crop nutrients need a nutrient hopper within one tile.

Material.PhobosEvaporiteCrust_descriptio: A chunk of salt-streaked clay from a dried brine vein: rock salt, potassium chloride, sodium sulfate and carbonate, a little magnesium phosphate and a trace of fluoride salt, the minerals NASA's OSIRIS-REx team found in samples from the asteroid Bennu. Leach it in a Lixivar LC-3 for potassium sulfate and phosphate. The government kiosks buy it like other ore.
Material.PhobosPotassiumSulfate_descript: 700 g of potassium sulfate crystallised from an evaporite crust. A fertiliser salt: in the LC-3, blend one with two struvite for Groundwork makeup salts, or one with a struvite, an Epsom salt and an ammonium sulfate for crop nutrients.
Material.PhobosPhosphateConcentrate_desc: 250 g of sodium magnesium phosphate washed out of an evaporite crust. With a little ammonia and water the LC-3 turns it into struvite.
Material.PhobosLeachedResidue_descriptio: 6.8 kg of washed clay and magnesium carbonate left from an evaporite crust. Bake it in a V4 refinery to collect its carbon dioxide in a linked store.
Material.PhobosStruvite_description: 430 g of struvite, a slow-release magnesium ammonium phosphate fertiliser. In the LC-3, blend two with one potassium sulfate for Groundwork makeup salts, or one into each batch of crop nutrients.
Material.PhobosBrineSaltCake_description: 2.25 kg of the crust's sodium salts: rock salt, sodium carbonate and a trace of sodium fluoride. Sodium harms crops, so it is no fertiliser. Nothing recovers it.
Material.PhobosCausticRemainder_descript: 70 g of sodium hydroxide left after making struvite. A caustic waste; nothing more can be recovered from it.
Material.PhobosCalcinedResidue_descripti: 6.54 kg of baked clay and magnesium oxide, left after carbon dioxide was driven out of washed residue. Nothing more can be recovered from it.
Acid.name: Sulfuric Acid Tank
Acid.details: A {3} x {3} acid tank with a second shell to catch leaks. Weighs {0:F0} kg empty and holds {1:F0} kg of concentrated sulfuric acid. An SA-3 fills it; an LC-3 uses its acid. Place them touching or join them with an acid line under or beside both. Stations also sell acid under Bulk supplies. Damage traps acid in the outer shell but releases poisonous mist into the room. Keep crew clear. Uses acid lines only; it cannot feed thrusters, gas filling stations or cabin air.

AcidLine.name: Acid Line
AcidLine.description: Lined line for concentrated sulfuric acid between acid tanks and the machines that fill or draw from them. Lay it tile by tile on intact floor until it runs under or right beside each acid tank and each machine that uses one; everything of that sort it touches joins the same line, and touching equipment joins without it. Shares a tile with other kinds of line. Once joined to a tank it fills with about 0.9 kg of acid a tile and keeps it. Damage lets a trace of it into the room as mist, so keep the crew clear; drain it into a canister before repair or taking it up.

Material.PhobosSulfideNodule_description: A dark, brassy chunk of troilite (iron sulfide) with streaks of schreibersite, a nickel-iron phosphide, of the kind found in iron meteorites. Roast it in a Lixivar SA-3 for sulfuric and phosphoric acid. The government kiosks buy it like other ore.
Material.PhobosPhosphoricAcidFlask_descr: 515 g of phosphoric acid caught from a roasted nodule, in a sealed flask: the phosphorus of three struvite. Corrosive. The LC-3 turns it into struvite with three Epsom salt and ammonia.
Material.PhobosRoastedCalcine_descriptio: 9.535 kg of iron and nickel oxides and rock left when a sulfide nodule is roasted. Nothing recovers it.
Material.PhobosEpsomSalt_description: 432 g of Epsom salt (magnesium sulfate) crystallised from olivine dissolved in sulfuric acid. Magnesium for crops: the LC-3 takes three with a phosphoric acid flask for struvite, and one in each batch of crop nutrients.
Material.PhobosAmmoniumSulfate_descripti: 232 g of ammonium sulfate, a nitrogen fertiliser salt made beside struvite on the acid route. The LC-3 blends one into each batch of crop nutrients.
Material.PhobosOlivineLeachCake_descript: 14.33 kg of silica gel, iron sulfate and undissolved rock, with the Epsom liquor soaked into them, left when the LC-3 leaches olivine. Nothing recovers it.
